title: The Miracle Unfolding in Mississippi Schools

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件你最珍贵的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成一个美丽的、有50年历史的古董移动流行博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼推出的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittreweff.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是娜塔莉·基特罗夫。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In the middle of a crisis for American education, with reading and math scores down across much of the country, one place has managed a stunning turnaround.
sentences.zh: 在美式教育陷入危机、全国大部分地区的阅读和数学成绩都在下降的时候，有一个地方设法实现了惊人的扭转。

sentences.en: Mississippi, one of the poorest states in America.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州，美国最贫穷的州之一。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Sarah Mervash on how Mississippi may have pulled off an educational miracle and what a deep red state could teach us.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事莎拉·默瓦什将探讨密西西比州是如何创造教育奇迹的，以及这个坚定的红州能教给我们什么。

sentences.en: about how to educate our kids.
sentences.zh: 关于如何教育我们的孩子。

sentences.en: It's Friday, April 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月10日，星期五。

sentences.en: Sarah, you've been spending time looking into what is being called the Mississippi miracle, this unthinkable improvement in the state's schooling.
sentences.zh: 莎拉，你一直在花时间调查所谓的“密西西比奇迹”，也就是该州学校发生的这种不可思议的改善。

sentences.en: I want to start by asking you first to just lay out what that improvement has actually looked like, the scale and the scope of this turnaround.
sentences.zh: 我想先请你大致介绍一下这种改善究竟是什么样的，这次转变的规模和范围如何。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's significant.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是非常显著的。

sentences.en: I'll start with just a few stats.
sentences.zh: 我先从几个统计数据开始讲起。

sentences.en: As recently as 2013, Mississippi ranked 49th in the country for education, particularly for young kids learning how to read.
sentences.zh: 就在2013年，密西西比州的教育在全美排名第49位，特别是针对学习阅读的低龄儿童。

sentences.en: 49th.
sentences.zh: 第49位。

sentences.en: 49th.
sentences.zh: 第49位。

sentences.en: No one wants to be 49.
sentences.zh: 没有人想当第49名。

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so that's a result that in some ways seemed predictable and even inevitable because Mississippi is a pretty poor state.
sentences.zh: 所以这个结果在某种程度上似乎是可以预见的，甚至是不可避免的，因为密西西比州是一个相当贫穷的州。

sentences.en: It doesn't spend a lot on education.
sentences.zh: 它在教育上花钱不多。

sentences.en: But slowly but surely, they started turning things around.
sentences.zh: 但他们慢慢地、稳步地开始扭转局面。

sentences.en: By 2019, they were about in line with the national average.
sentences.zh: 到2019年，他们的水平大致与全国平均水平相当。

sentences.en: And now they are a top 10 state for fourth graders learning how to read.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们已经成为四年级学生阅读水平排名前十的州。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think something even more impressive is if you adjust for poverty in other demographics like race,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为更令人印象深刻的是，如果你根据贫困率和种族等其他人口统计数据进行调整，

sentences.en: Mississippi is the number one place in the country for fourth graders learning reading and math and the number one state for eighth grade math.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州是全国四年级学生阅读和数学学习的第一名，也是八年级数学的第一名。

sentences.en: Okay, just explain that for me.
sentences.zh: 好的，请为我解释一下。

sentences.en: When you say when you adjust for poverty, it's number one for these metrics.
sentences.zh: 当你说的根据贫困情况进行调整时，它在这些指标上是第一名。

sentences.en: What do you mean exactly by that?
sentences.zh: 你这具体是什么意思？

sentences.en: Some of the best states that traditionally are seen as having the best education are the richest states, places like Massachusetts or New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 传统上被认为拥有最好教育的一些最好的州是最富有的州，比如马萨诸塞州或新泽西州，

sentences.en: because rich kids just score higher.
sentences.zh: 因为有钱人的孩子就是能考得更高。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But if you adjust for the student population that they're serving, so how does a state serve its poor kids or if it has a lot of kids who are learning English?
sentences.zh: 但是如果你根据他们所服务的学生群体进行调整，比如一个州如何为其贫困儿童服务，或者它是否有大量正在学习英语的孩子？

sentences.en: So when you look at the students that it has, how does the state do?
sentences.zh: 所以当你看看它拥有的学生时，这个州表现如何？

sentences.en: Mississippi does really well.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州做得非常好。

sentences.en: Poor kids in Mississippi are scoring better on national tests in fourth grade than poor kids in almost any other state.
sentences.zh: 在四年级全国测试中，密西西比州的贫困儿童的成绩比几乎其他任何州的贫困儿童都要好。

sentences.en: So basically what that's telling me is that Mississippi is one of the best places in the country for a poor child to get an education.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上告诉我的是，对贫困儿童来说，密西西比州是全国接受教育最好的地方之一。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's pretty remarkable.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这非常了不起。

sentences.en: And all that is happening, of course, in a context where America's schools are not doing well, right, on the whole.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切发生的时候，当然，整个美国的学校表现并不好，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, the trends are bad.
sentences.zh: 比如，趋势很糟糕。

sentences.en: Test scores generally are down across the board.
sentences.zh: 测试成绩总体上全面下降。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think this is something that would maybe surprise people who have heard, oh, it's pandemic losses.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这可能会让那些听说过“哦，这是疫情造成的损失”的人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Actually, this decline started going back to 2015.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种下降从2015年就开始了。

sentences.en: Things started to take a bit of a turn.
sentences.zh: 情况开始出现一些转变。

sentences.en: And this decline was basically driven by the lowest performing students.
sentences.zh: 而这种下降基本上是由表现最差的学生驱动的。

sentences.en: So our bottom 25 percent of students have just been dropping off for about a decade or more.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们排在后25%的学生在大约十年或更长的时间里一直在退步。

sentences.en: And in reading in particular, the declines have continued since COVID.
sentences.zh: 特别是在阅读方面，自新冠疫情以来，下降趋势一直在继续。

sentences.en: So things are just continuing to trend downward.
sentences.zh: 所以情况只是继续呈下降趋势。

sentences.en: And one of the things that got me really interested in Mississippi was that Mississippi is one of the only states that's defying that trend,
sentences.zh: 让我对密西西比州真正感兴趣的事情之一是，密西西比州是少数几个逆势而上的州之一，

sentences.en: either helping its lowest performing students hold steady or even helping them improve during this time frame.
sentences.zh: 在这个时期，它要么帮助表现最差的学生保持稳定，要么甚至帮助他们在此时期取得进步。

sentences.en: Okay, so I have to imagine that much of the country is looking at what happened in Mississippi and trying to figure out how they did it,
sentences.zh: 好吧，我可以想象全国大部分地区都在关注密西西比州发生的事情，并试图弄清楚他们是怎么做到的，

sentences.en: which is exactly what you set out to do in your reporting, Sarah.
sentences.zh: 这正是你在报道中着手要做的事情，莎拉。

sentences.en: So what did you learn?
sentences.zh: 那么你学到了什么？

sentences.en: Like, how did they do it?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Well, there wasn't a magic bullet, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不幸的是，并没有什么灵丹妙药。

sentences.en: Everyone wants there to be one simple thing.
sentences.zh: 每个人都希望有一个简单的方法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And what I found is that it was several different factors.
sentences.zh: 我发现这是几个不同因素共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: And at a high level, what that looked like was the state taking a much more aggressive,
sentences.zh: 从宏观层面来看，这意味着州政府采取了更加积极主动、

sentences.en: hands-on role to education and sort of telling districts what to do.
sentences.zh: 亲力亲为的教育角色，有点像在告诉各学区该怎么做。

sentences.en: And part of that was about how they taught young children how to read, but it also was about accountability and support.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分关于他们如何教小孩子阅读，但也关乎问责制和支持。

sentences.en: So I think that was a really crucial aspect of what Mississippi did is they were actually holding schools accountable,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为密西西比州所做的一个极其关键的方面是，他们确实在追究学校的责任，

sentences.en: but they were also, like, getting in there and offering support.
sentences.zh: 但他们也深入基层提供支持。

sentences.en: And that support was also telling schools what to do.
sentences.zh: 这种支持也包括告诉学校该做什么。

sentences.en: And when did this start?
sentences.zh: 这始于什么时候？

sentences.en: When did this turn around?
sentences.zh: 这个转变是什么时候开始的？

sentences.en: When did these interventions begin?
sentences.zh: 这些干预措施是什么时候开始的？

sentences.en: So a lot of this dates back to 2013.
sentences.zh: 所以这很多可以追溯到2013年。

sentences.en: People in Mississippi have been trying to make progress on education for a while and making some changes.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州的人们一直在努力取得教育方面的进展并进行一些改变。

sentences.en: But when you're 49th in the country, it's sort of like even, you know, from a business standpoint,
sentences.zh: 但当你在全国排名第49位时，这就有点像，你知道的，从商业的角度来看，

sentences.en: when you look at the future outlook of your state, you've got, like, Republican-led legislature and business leaders and people all agreeing, thinking we've got to do something.
sentences.zh: 当你审视你所在州的未来前景时，你有共和党领导的立法机构、商界领袖和人们都表示赞同，认为我们必须做点什么。

sentences.en: This is a crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一场危机。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so what they decide to do is they pass a big sweeping piece of legislation that focuses on changing how young kids learn how to read.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决定通过一项大规模、全面的立法，重点改变低龄儿童学习阅读的方式。

sentences.en: I'm Sarah Murbosch.
sentences.zh: 我是莎拉·默博施。

sentences.en: I'm the reporter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的记者。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: So to really see this in person and get a sense of it myself, I went to a school called Hazelhurst Elementary.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了亲眼见证并亲自感受这一点，我去了黑兹尔赫斯特小学。

sentences.en: And it's in a rural community south of Jackson, which is the state capital.
sentences.zh: 它位于杰克逊以南的一个乡村社区，杰克逊是州首府。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And back in 2015, just 12 percent of students at the school were reading on grade level.
sentences.zh: 早在2015年，该校仅有12%的学生达到年级阅读水平。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And today they have clawed and fought to get that figure to 35 percent.
sentences.zh: 而今天，他们通过奋斗将这一数字提升到了35%。

sentences.en: Impressive.
sentences.zh: 令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's really, really hard to dramatically improve test scores, particularly for poor students who have a lot going on in their home lives.
sentences.zh: 显著提高测试成绩真的非常非常困难，特别是对于那些家庭生活有很多变故的贫困学生来说。

sentences.en: But I don't think anyone, including the principal, would argue that it's, you know, it's OK to have just 35 percent of students reading on grade level.
sentences.zh: 但我认为没有人，包括校长，会认为只有35%的学生达到年级阅读水平就可以了。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But it's real, real progress.
sentences.zh: 但这真的是真正的进步。

sentences.en: So how did they do it?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: OK, boys and girls, I need your attention.
sentences.zh: 好了，男孩女孩们，请注意。

sentences.en: I need your eyes on me.
sentences.zh: 看着我。

sentences.en: One, two.
sentences.zh: 一，二。

sentences.en: So this big piece of legislation really changed the way that children were taught to read.
sentences.zh: 所以这项重大的立法真正改变了儿童学习阅读的方式。

sentences.en: And if you go into a school like Hazelhurst, you're not going to see, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你走进像黑兹尔赫斯特这样的学校，你不会看到，你知道的，

sentences.en: kids off in the corner on their own, sort of nestled up with a book, just sort of absorbed in a picture book.
sentences.zh: 孩子们独自坐在角落里，手里拿着一本书，完全沉浸在一本图画书里。

sentences.en: Really what you're going to see is like what I saw, which is.
sentences.zh: 你真正会看到的就像我看到的那样。

sentences.en: So my word would be what?
sentences.zh: 所以我的词会是什么？

sentences.en: Nineteen.
sentences.zh: 十九。

sentences.en: Blamelessness.
sentences.zh: 无可指责。

sentences.en: Second graders sounding out words together, blamelessness.
sentences.zh: 二年级学生一起拼读单词，无可指责。

sentences.en: Do it again.
sentences.zh: 再来一遍。

sentences.en: Blamelessness.
sentences.zh: 无可指责。

sentences.en: Blamelessness.
sentences.zh: 无可指责。

sentences.en: Good job.
sentences.zh: 干得好。

sentences.en: And so they explicitly teach kids how to sound out words.
sentences.zh: 所以他们明确教导孩子们如何拼读单词。

sentences.en: That's called phonics.
sentences.zh: 这被称为自然拼读法。

sentences.en: But they also teach things like vocabulary, like explicitly.
sentences.zh: 但他们也教诸如词汇之类的东西，而且是明确地教。

sentences.en: It's not just assume that you're going to know what that word is and that passage you're reading.
sentences.zh: 不仅是假设你会知道你在读的那段文字里的那个词是什么意思。

sentences.en: So I went into, I think it was a second or third grade classroom.
sentences.zh: 所以我走进了，我想是一个二年级或三年级的教室。

sentences.en: And I remember they were reading a passage and they were discussing what is the meaning of complain.
sentences.zh: 我记得他们在读一段文章，并讨论“抱怨”是什么意思。

sentences.en: The next word is complain.
sentences.zh: 下一个词是抱怨。

sentences.en: Can you say complain?
sentences.zh: 你能说抱怨吗？

sentences.en: Complain.
sentences.zh: 抱怨。

sentences.en: And that was one of the words, the vocabulary words that day.
sentences.zh: 那是那天众多词汇中的一个。

sentences.en: Very important to know.
sentences.zh: 了解这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: The kids were, they had many complaints.
sentences.zh: 孩子们有很多抱怨。

sentences.en: They were very animated and very into it.
sentences.zh: 他们非常活跃，非常投入。

sentences.en: Anybody else complain about something?
sentences.zh: 还有人抱怨什么吗？

sentences.en: Tyler.
sentences.zh: 泰勒。

sentences.en: Will my dog make it too much worse in the house?
sentences.zh: 我的狗会不会把家里弄得更糟？

sentences.en: Oh, Lord, I don't even like animals.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我甚至不喜欢动物。

sentences.en: Thank God I don't have these.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地我没有这些。

sentences.en: So that's actually a significant change from just sort of reading for the love of reading and developing a love of reading and maybe adding in some phonics as it comes up.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是一个重大转变，从单纯为了对阅读的热爱而阅读、培养对阅读的热爱，并在出现时可能加入一些自然拼读，

sentences.en: But it's explicit teaching and it's direct.
sentences.zh: 变成了明确的教学和直接的指导。

sentences.en: It's not just implied.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是暗示。

sentences.en: And how did the law make this happen?
sentences.zh: 那法律是怎么做到这一点的？

sentences.en: Like, how do you, if you're a state government, mandate an approach to teaching reading?
sentences.zh: 如果你是州政府，你如何强制推行一种教授阅读的方法？

sentences.en: How do you control what teachers do in their classrooms?
sentences.zh: 你如何控制教师在教室里的行为？

sentences.en: Well, Mississippi was basically at the forefront of this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，密西西比州基本上走在了这方面的最前沿。

sentences.en: Lots of states have since done this.
sentences.zh: 许多州后来都效仿了这一点。

sentences.en: But what Mississippi did is it put a huge focus on how to train teachers, how to teach reading.
sentences.zh: 但密西西比州所做的是，它高度聚焦于如何培训教师以及如何教授阅读。

sentences.en: They were not just letting teachers teach willy-nilly however they learned in school or whatever their teacher done in the hall taught them.
sentences.zh: 他们不再任由教师随心所欲地教学，无论他们在学校里学到了什么，或者大厅里的其他老师教了他们什么。

sentences.en: The state was saying this is the best practice.
sentences.zh: 州政府在说这就是最佳实践。

sentences.en: But then they also, if you're in the bottom 25 percent of schools, they send a literacy coach into your school.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们还规定，如果你处于排名后25%的学校，他们就会派一名识字教练去你的学校。

sentences.en: What is a literacy coach?
sentences.zh: 什么是识字教练？

sentences.en: It is not a coach for the students.
sentences.zh: 它不是学生的教练。

sentences.en: It is a coach for the teachers.
sentences.zh: 它是老师的教练。

sentences.en: And so it's basically like an amplifier and sending the best practices out into the system to say, this is how you teach reading.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上就像一个放大器，将最佳实践发送到整个系统中，说，这就是你教阅读的方法。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So in my story, I'm not seeing the story that we're on, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在我的报道中，我没有看到我们正在进行的报道，对吧？

sentences.en: And when I was there, I observed the coach in action.
sentences.zh: 当我在那里时，我观察了教练的实际工作。

sentences.en: And there's a lot that goes into it.
sentences.zh: 其中有很多学问。

sentences.en: Some of it is the coach actually leading a lesson in the classroom and the teacher watching the coach do it.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分是教练实际在教室里上一堂课，老师看着教练这样做。

sentences.en: But it can also be in real time, small corrections.
sentences.zh: 但也可以是实时的微小纠正。

sentences.en: The coach, when I was there, corrected one of the teachers who was mispronouncing a word.
sentences.zh: 我在那里时，教练纠正了一位发音错误的老师。

sentences.en: She was mispronouncing the word tortoise.
sentences.zh: 她把乌龟（tortoise）这个词发错了音。

sentences.en: I had the tortoise, which was my turtle, and I had my hair.
sentences.zh: 我有那只乌龟，它是我的宠物，我还有我的头发。

sentences.en: And the literacy coach just walked right up to her and just whispered in her ear and corrected her in the moment.
sentences.zh: 而识字指导员直接走到她跟前，在她耳边低声细语，当场纠正了她。

sentences.en: My tortoise, my tortoise, okay?
sentences.zh: 我的乌龟，我的乌龟，好吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You know, it's like a real-time coach for how to do your job.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就像是一个实时教练，指导你如何做好工作。

sentences.en: And what do teachers think about this?
sentences.zh: 老师们对这个怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, I was surprised.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很吃惊。

sentences.en: I thought they might be a little prickly.
sentences.zh: 我以为他们可能会有点难对付。

sentences.en: But at the school that I went to, they loved it.
sentences.zh: 但在我去的那所学校，他们非常喜欢。

sentences.en: Like, they loved it.
sentences.zh: 真的，他们太喜欢了。

sentences.en: And I talked to some of the teachers, and they were just thirsty for the knowledge and for the help.
sentences.zh: 我和一些老师聊过，他们对知识和帮助有着极度的渴望。

sentences.en: And I think if you could just have a mentor, basically, to help you every time you get frustrated or confused,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你能有一个导师，基本上在你每次感到沮丧或困惑时都能帮你一把，

sentences.en: and that person was not there in a punitive way, and that's very important.
sentences.zh: 并且这个人不是带着惩罚的意味去的，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: In Mississippi, they are state employees, but they're not there to punish.
sentences.zh: 在密西西比州，他们是州雇员，但他们不是去惩罚人的。

sentences.en: They're really there to mentor and coach and spread best practices.
sentences.zh: 他们真的是去指导、训练并传播最佳实践的。

sentences.en: Like, hallelujah.
sentences.zh: 简直就像谢天谢地一样。

sentences.en: Like, I would love if someone could just help me every time I was struggling with a story.
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果我每次为一个故事苦恼时都有人能帮我，我可太喜欢了。

sentences.en: Sounds awesome.
sentences.zh: 听起来棒极了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Honestly.
sentences.zh: 说实话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And another thing that they did is the state took a stronger role in taking a top-down approach to curriculum, which is not always popular.
sentences.zh: 他们做的另一件事是，州政府在课程方面采取了更强势、自上而下的方法，这并不总是受欢迎的。

sentences.en: And so what they did is basically say, like, here are the five or six curriculums that we think are high quality
sentences.zh: 所以他们做的基本上就是说，比如，这里是我们认为高质量的五、六种课程，

sentences.en: and approved for use in Mississippi for teaching reading, for example.
sentences.zh: 并且批准在密西西比州用于教授阅读等。

sentences.en: And so this was actually very eye-opening to me because at this school that I visited, they had previously been using a different kind of curriculum that was an intervention.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上让我大开眼界，因为在我参观的这所学校里，他们以前一直在使用一种不同的干预类课程。

sentences.en: So if a child is behind and they're giving a special curriculum, like, all kids were getting that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果一个孩子落后了，他们会获得专门的课程，这就像所有孩子都在接受这种课程一样。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Because a lot of kids at the school were behind.
sentences.zh: 因为学校里很多孩子都落后了。

sentences.en: And that is a problem because that means that kids are not getting access to the grade-level content
sentences.zh: 这是个问题，因为这意味着孩子们接触不到年级水平的内容，

sentences.en: at sort of the highest level that they would be expected to perform at the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 达不到他们在年底时被期望达到的最高水平。

sentences.en: And so the state coaches and others helped recognize that and said, hey, we actually need to adjust this.
sentences.zh: 因此，州指导员和其他人帮助认识到了这一点，并表示，嘿，我们实际上需要调整一下。

sentences.en: And so we're going to switch to one of the state-vetted curriculuMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要转而使用州里审核通过的课程之一。

sentences.en: And Sarah, when you said earlier that Mississippi was also holding schools accountable, what did you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 萨拉，你刚才说密西西比州也在追究学校的责任，这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, around the same time that they passed this big 2013 legislation, they also changed their accountability system for schools.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大约在他们通过2013年这项重大立法的同时，他们也改变了学校的问责制系统。

sentences.en: So they did two things.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做了两件事。

sentences.en: One, they raised the standards for what it means to be proficient in reading or math.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们提高了对阅读或数学达到熟练水平的要求标准。

sentences.en: So they basically raised the bar for what kids need to know.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上为孩子们需要掌握的知识抬高了门槛。

sentences.en: And then they also changed the way that schools were graded and held accountable.
sentences.zh: 然后他们还改变了学校评分和追究责任的方式。

sentences.en: And all of this talk about accountability might bring back memories of something called no child left behind.
sentences.zh: 所有关于问责制的讨论可能会勾起人们对被称为“不让一个孩子掉队”的回忆。

sentences.en: You know, a huge percentage of children in poverty can't read at grade level.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，很大一部分处于贫困中的儿童无法达到年级阅读水平。

sentences.en: That's not right in America.
sentences.zh: 这在美利坚是不对的。

sentences.en: We're going to win the war overseas and we need to win the war against illiteracy here at home as well.
sentences.zh: 我们要赢得海外的战争，同样也需要在国内赢得消除文盲的战争。

sentences.en: And so this bill.
sentences.zh: 所以这项法案。

sentences.en: No Child Left Behind, of course, is the George W.
sentences.zh: “不让一个孩子掉队”当然是乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush era policy that went into effect in 2002.
sentences.zh: 布什时期的政策，于2002年生效。

sentences.en: And if you were growing up in the United States in that time, like I was, and you were taking tests, that was no child left behind, like what was the proficiency of your school.
sentences.zh: 如果你在那时像我一样在美国长大，并且正在参加考试，那就是“不让一个孩子掉队”，比如你所在学校的熟练程度如何。

sentences.en: So this bill focuses on reading.
sentences.zh: 所以这项法案侧重于阅读。

sentences.en: It sets a grand goal for the country.
sentences.zh: 它为国家设定了一个宏伟的目标。

sentences.en: Our children will be reading by the third grade.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子将在三年级时学会阅读。

sentences.en: That's not an impossible goal.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个不可能实现的目标。

sentences.en: It's a goal we must meet if we want every child to succeed.
sentences.zh: 如果我们希望每个孩子都成功，这是一个我们必须达到的目标。

sentences.en: And so what that law did is it literally set the goal that every child in America would be proficient in reading and math.
sentences.zh: 所以那项法律的作用是，它字面意义上设定了一个目标，即美国每个孩子都将在阅读和数学上达到熟练水平。

sentences.en: Because the only way to determine whether a child is reading at grade level is to have accountability in our school systeMs.
sentences.zh: 因为确定一个孩子是否达到年级阅读水平的唯一方法，就是在我们的学校系统中建立问责制。

sentences.en: And that's the basic strategy of No Child Left Behind.
sentences.zh: 这就是“不让一个孩子掉队”的基本策略。

sentences.en: It says, here's some money.
sentences.zh: 它说，这里有一些钱。

sentences.en: We expect you to teach.
sentences.zh: 我们期望你们教学。

sentences.en: We want to measure to determine if you are teaching.
sentences.zh: 我们想要进行衡量，以确定你们是否在教学。

sentences.en: We look forward to patting you on the back.
sentences.zh: 我们期待着拍拍你们的背以示鼓励。

sentences.en: But if you're not teaching a child the basics, then we expect you to change before it is too late.
sentences.zh: 但如果你们没有教给孩子基础知识，那么我们期望在为时已晚之前你们能做出改变。

sentences.en: And if I remember correctly, this law was incredibly unpopular.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，这项法律极不受欢迎。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it was very contentious.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，它非常有争议。

sentences.en: Teachers and parents alike grew frustrated at certain points with it.
sentences.zh: 老师和家长在某些时候都对它感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And there was a pushback that there was just too much testing.
sentences.zh: 并且有一种强烈反对的声音，认为考试实在是太多了。

sentences.en: Teachers were teaching to the teSt.
sentences.zh: 老师们为了应试而教。

sentences.en: That they were taking time away from other important subjects like art or music or social studies.
sentences.zh: 这占用了其他重要学科的时间，比如美术、音乐或社会科学。

sentences.en: So eventually it just becomes so unpopular and there's so much pushback that in 2015, No Child Left Behind is repealed and replaced with a different law,
sentences.zh: 所以最终它变得如此不受欢迎，反对声如此巨大，以至于在2015年，“不让一个孩子掉队”被废除，并被另一项法律取代，

sentences.en: the Every Student Succeeds Act under President Obama.
sentences.zh: 即奥巴马总统任内的《每一个学生都成功法案》。

sentences.en: And so in 2015 and even a little bit before that, states start to sort of move away from accountability as the mantra in education.
sentences.zh: 所以在2015年甚至在那之前的一点时间里，各州开始逐渐不再将问责制奉为教育界的金科玉律。

sentences.en: But Mississippi embraces accountability.
sentences.zh: 但密西西比州拥抱了问责制。

sentences.en: What's their logic?
sentences.zh: 他们的逻辑是什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这么做了。

sentences.en: It's sort of like No Child Left Behind but with a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 这有点像“不让一个孩子掉队”，但带有一点转折。

sentences.en: So Mississippi leaders felt like it was really important to have some way to see how schools are doing and help parents to decide what was a good school, what's not.
sentences.zh: 所以密西西比州的领导人觉得，有一些方法来观察学校的表现，并帮助家长决定什么是好学校、什么不是，这非常重要。

sentences.en: And so what that looks like in Mississippi now is that schools get an A through F letter rating.
sentences.zh: 所以在现在的密西西比州，看起来就是学校会得到A到F的字母等级评定。

sentences.en: And what goes into that is not just, you know, how much do students know at the end of the year?
sentences.zh: 其中包含的内容不仅是，你知道的，学生在年底掌握了多少知识？

sentences.en: Are they on grade level?
sentences.zh: 他们达到年级水平了吗？

sentences.en: But they also take into account growth.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还将进步幅度考虑在内。

sentences.en: How much are the students improving throughout the year?
sentences.zh: 学生们在这一年里进步了多少？

sentences.en: Where do they start?
sentences.zh: 他们从哪里开始？

sentences.en: Where do they end up?
sentences.zh: 他们最终达到了什么水平？

sentences.en: And really importantly, they double count the improvement of students in the bottom 25%.
sentences.zh: 非常重要的是，他们对处于后25%的学生的进步给予双倍计分。

sentences.en: So schools are motivated not just to help their top students or their middle students who are on the verge of proficiency,
sentences.zh: 所以学校不仅有动力去帮助顶尖学生或处在及格边缘的中等生，

sentences.en: but they're motivated to help all students because they get credit for helping all students and they get double credit for helping their lowest performing students.
sentences.zh: 而且他们有动力去帮助所有学生，因为帮助所有学生可以获得积分，而帮助表现最差的学生可以获得双倍积分。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: So what's happening here is Mississippi is deciding how well each school is doing, not just by looking at the absolute scores that these kids are getting,
sentences.zh: 所以这里发生的事情是，密西西比州不仅通过查看这些孩子的绝对分数来决定每个学校的表现，

sentences.en: but by looking at the change in those scores.
sentences.zh: 而是通过查看这些分数的变动来决定。

sentences.en: They're measuring progress, essentially.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，他们在衡量进步。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we know teachers hated being graded on test scores during No Child Left Behind.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，在“不让一个孩子掉队”期间，老师们讨厌根据考试成绩被评定等级。

sentences.en: How did teachers and students that you talked to in Hazlehurst feel about this focus on test scores, this No Child Left Behind with a twist, as you put it?
sentences.zh: 你在黑兹尔赫斯特交谈过的老师和学生，对这种聚焦于考试成绩的做法，也就是你所说的带有一点转折的“不让一个孩子掉队”，有什么感受？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, some of the criticisms of No Child Left Behind can still apply to Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对“不让一个孩子掉队”的一些批评仍然可以适用于密西西比州。

sentences.en: There is a big testing culture.
sentences.zh: 这里存在着浓厚的考试文化。

sentences.en: At the school that I visited, students were taking tests every two weeks, like even more than the state recommended.
sentences.zh: 在我参观的那所学校里，学生每两周就要参加一次考试，甚至比州里推荐的还要频繁。

sentences.en: Yikes.
sentences.zh: 哎呀。

sentences.en: But they, you know, the school felt like they couldn't afford to wait any longer to see, you know, how kids were doing.
sentences.zh: 但他们，你知道的，学校觉得他们等不及看孩子们表现如何了。

sentences.en: And even health class was sort of like more reading instruction and vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 甚至健康课也变成了更多的阅读指导和词汇学习。

sentences.en: So some of those same criticisms still exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些同样的批评依然存在。

sentences.en: The teachers, I think, in some ways did feel some measure of pressure to deliver on the results.
sentences.zh: 我认为，老师们在某些方面确实感到了交付成果的压力。

sentences.en: But I also observed, you know, in the interactions that I saw with the kids,
sentences.zh: 但我也观察到，你知道的，在我看到的与孩子们的互动中，

sentences.en: just how much joy and satisfaction and dignity they felt in the learning itself that I don't think we can take for granted.
sentences.zh: 他们在学习本身中感受到了多少快乐、满足和尊严，这是我们不能视为理所当然的。

sentences.en: I saw one little girl in second grade who was, you know, coaching another kid on how to pronounce a word.
sentences.zh: 我看到一个二年级的小女孩，你知道的，正在指导另一个孩子如何发音。

sentences.en: And so they're teaching each other.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在互相教导。

sentences.en: And I did some interviews with fifth graders.
sentences.zh: 我采访了一些五年级的学生。

sentences.zh: 约翰尼，你多大了？

sentences.zh: 好的，那就是五年级。

sentences.zh: 这里每个人都在五年级吗？

sentences.zh: 是的，先生。

sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Who, you know, talked about, you know, how they felt about the testing.
sentences.zh: 谁，你知道的，谈论了，你知道的，他们对考试的感受。

sentences.en: Some of them felt some pressure.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人感到了一些压力。

sentences.en: But then this 10-year-old named Johnny described what I thought was so profound.
sentences.zh: 但接着这个名叫约翰尼的10岁男孩描述了我认为非常深刻的事情。

sentences.en: He told me, this will stick with me for a long time.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，这件事会在我脑海里留存很久。

sentences.en: He talked about tracking his own testing data.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了追踪自己的测试数据。

sentences.zh: 你们在成长。

sentences.zh: 作为学生，你们有关于自己在班上表现如何的信息吗？

sentences.en: Like, I like it how, like, if I make a low grade, on the other grades, if I make it higher, it's like staircases that go up.
sentences.zh: 就像，我喜欢这样，如果我得了低分，在其他成绩上，如果我考得更高，就像是向上延伸的楼梯。

sentences.zh: 就像搭梯子一样。

sentences.zh: 你喜欢它，因为它像楼梯？

sentences.en: Because if you start out, you know, but down here, when you're going up, that feels good?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你开始时，你知道的，在下面，当你往上走的时候，那感觉很好？

sentences.zh: 就像一根金属条。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这些是有史以来最可爱的采访。

sentences.en: Fifth graders, I'm very jealous.
sentences.zh: 五年级的学生，我非常嫉妒。

sentences.zh: 抛开阅读不谈，最喜欢的部分是什么？

sentences.zh: 你一天中最喜欢学校的哪个部分？

sentences.zh: 什么都可以。

sentences.en: Eat it.
sentences.zh: 吃东西。

sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 所以密西西比州正在指导其老师如何教学。

sentences.en: It's grading schools based on the improvement that they're making in the kids' test scores.
sentences.zh: 它根据孩子们考试成绩的提升来对学校进行评分。

sentences.en: Are those the main ingredients to this Mississippi approach?
sentences.zh: 这些是密西西比方法的 主要成分吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's one other thing, and that is Mississippi is also holding kids accountable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有一件事，那就是密西西比州也在追究孩子们的责任。

sentences.en: And that's one of the most controversial and most debated things that they have done.
sentences.zh: 这是他们做过的最具争议和讨论最多的事情之一。

sentences.en: Okay, Sarah, before we get to the controversy surrounding this element of the approach, explain to me, how exactly does the state hold kids accountable?
sentences.zh: 好的，萨拉，在我们探讨这种方法中引发争议的环节之前，请先给我解释一下，州政府究竟是如何追究孩子们责任的？

sentences.en: Well, that 2013 big piece of legislation, a big part of it said that if kids don't know how to read by the end of third grade, they're holding kids back.
sentences.zh: 嗯，2013年的那项重大立法中，很大一部分内容规定，如果孩子们在三年级结束时还不会阅读，就会被留级。

sentences.en: And so every year, about six to nine percent of Mississippi third graders are held back.
sentences.zh: 因此，每年大约有百分之六到百分之九的密西西比州三年级学生会留级。

sentences.en: And there are certain exceptions, but more or less, if you can't learn to read by the end of the year, you can't move on.
sentences.zh: 当然也有一些例外情况，但大体上说，如果你在年底前学不会阅读，就不能升学。

sentences.en: And why is that controversial?
sentences.zh: 为什么这会引起争议呢？

sentences.en: Explain that part.
sentences.zh: 解释一下这部分。

sentences.en: Oh, all sorts of reasons.
sentences.zh: 哦，原因各种各样。

sentences.en: I mean, the emotional impact on kids.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对孩子们的心理冲击。

sentences.en: There's a lot of worry about what that's going to do to them long term and to see their peers move on.
sentences.zh: 人们非常担心这会对他们的长远发展产生什么影响，而且还要眼看着同龄人升学。

sentences.en: It also is just a lot of pressure.
sentences.zh: 而且这也带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the kids that I talked to almost like shuddered and wince thinking back to his third grade year and the amount of pressure that was for him about whether
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我采访过的一个孩子，回想起他的三年级以及当时面临的巨大压力时，几乎吓得发抖、畏缩，不知道

sentences.en: he was going to get to move on with his friends.
sentences.zh: 自己能不能和朋友们一起升学。

sentences.en: And then there's also just the question of whether it even helps them in the long term.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一个问题，就是这样做对他们从长远来看究竟有没有帮助。

sentences.en: There is some mixed evidence as to whether it really helps them by the time they get to later middle school or high school, for example.
sentences.zh: 对于这种做法到了他们上初中高中的时候是否真的有帮助，目前的证据褒贬不一。

sentences.en: And then there's, of course, just the realities of like who is going to get held back from a law like this.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有一些现实问题，比如像这样的法律究竟会让谁留级。

sentences.en: It's often not going to be tons and tons of kids from the affluent white district.
sentences.zh: 通常不会是那些富裕白人学区里的大量孩子。

sentences.en: There's going to be racial elements and class elements to who gets held back.
sentences.zh: 谁会留级，这里面存在着种族因素和阶层因素。

sentences.en: And so that's something that has come up.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一个被提出来的问题。

sentences.en: Whether this retention policy is actually what's driving Mississippi's success.
sentences.zh: 这种留级政策到底是不是密西西比州取得成功的动力。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: How do you mean?
sentences.zh: 此话怎讲？

sentences.en: Because some have argued that if you hold back kids in third grade, that their scores are going
sentences.zh: 因为有些人认为，如果你让学生在三年级留级，他们的成绩在四年级就会

sentences.en: to be higher in fourth grade, which is when this national test that sort of compares states measures kids' academic achievement.
sentences.zh: 更高，而四年级正是那种用于横向对比各州学生的全国性测试评估学生学业成绩的时候。

sentences.en: And so some have said that basically it's artificially inflating the scores.
sentences.zh: 因此，有人说这基本上是人为地抬高了成绩。

sentences.en: Because basically you're introducing potential selection bias, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你基本上引入了潜在的选择偏差，对吧？

sentences.en: You're taking out the lowest kids and giving them an extra year to learn.
sentences.zh: 你把成绩最差的孩子剔除出去，并给他们多学一年的时间。

sentences.en: And I spend a lot of time looking at this because, look, if you're going to look at a story about
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间来研究这个问题，因为你看，如果你要审视一篇关于

sentences.en: Mississippi, is that, you know, are they really doing well?
sentences.zh: 密西西比州的报道，那就是，你知道，他们真的做得很好吗？

sentences.en: And what I came to conclude is that, yes, the lowest performing third graders are held back each year and they do get an extra year of learning.
sentences.zh: 我得出的结论是，是的，每年表现最差的三年级学生都会留级，他们确实多了一年的学习时间。

sentences.en: And then they take the test the next year.
sentences.zh: 然后他们在第二年参加测试。

sentences.en: And part of the story here, I think, is about the extra help that they get.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这里的故事有一部分是关于他们获得的额外帮助。

sentences.en: They're not just retained without any help.
sentences.zh: 他们不只是在没有任何帮助的情况下被留级。

sentences.en: Like in Hazelhurst, for example, third graders get extra after-school help.
sentences.zh: 比如在黑兹尔赫斯特，三年级学生可以得到课后的额外辅导。

sentences.en: Kids can go to summer school.
sentences.zh: 孩子们可以去上暑期学校。

sentences.en: So they're sort of infused with extra support.
sentences.zh: 所以他们得到了各种额外支持的注入。

sentences.en: Like retention without support isn't good.
sentences.zh: 就像没有支持的留级是不可取的。

sentences.en: You can't just retain kids and be like, extra year and now you're going to be older and your friends are going to move on.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是让孩子留级，然后说，多读一年，现在你长大了，你的朋友们都升学了。

sentences.en: You have to have support to help them get there.
sentences.zh: 你必须提供支持来帮助他们达到标准。

sentences.en: Can I ask, how is Mississippi giving all of that support?
sentences.zh: 请问，密西西比州是如何提供所有这些支持的？

sentences.en: I mean, this is one of the poorest states in the country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是全国最贫穷的州之一。

sentences.en: How are they affording all of this?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么负担得起这一切？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they're on a budget.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，他们是在预算之内办事的。

sentences.en: Let's put it that way.
sentences.zh: 这么说吧。

sentences.en: Mississippi does have one of the lowest per student spending in the country.
sentences.zh: 密西西比州确实是全国每个学生平均教育支出最低的州之一。

sentences.en: They spend about $13,500 per student.
sentences.zh: 他们每个学生的支出大约是13500美元。

sentences.en: And that's compared to the national average, which is almost $18,000 per student.
sentences.zh: 而相比之下，全国平均水平几乎是每个学生18000美元。

sentences.en: And in states like New York, it's $29,000 per student.
sentences.zh: 在像纽约这样的州，则是每个学生29000美元。

sentences.en: So they're basically at or near the bottom in student spending.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的生均支出基本上处于垫底或接近垫底的水平。

sentences.en: And so this is a big question.
sentences.zh: 这就成了一个大问题。

sentences.en: How are they doing this?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: And so what I found when I went there is, look, I mean, the school that I went to is cash-strapped.
sentences.zh: 我实地探访后发现，你看，我去的那个学校资金极其短缺。

sentences.en: They recognize it and they're making academics their core.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到了这一点，并把学术作为核心。

sentences.en: That is what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们在做的事情。

sentences.en: And what the state does is they're spending a little more money.
sentences.zh: 州政府的做法是多花了一点钱。

sentences.en: But what they're doing is they're targeting it to specific things.
sentences.zh: 但他们做的是把钱用在刀刃上，针对特定项目进行投入。

sentences.en: So remember the literacy coaches I talked about?
sentences.zh: 还记得我提到过的识字辅导员吗？

sentences.en: That was an investment that the state made.
sentences.zh: 那是州政府的一项投资。

sentences.en: They also spent money to invest in preschool and expanding preschool so that more kids could be better prepared when they get to kindergarten.
sentences.zh: 他们还花钱投资学前教育并扩大其规模，以便让更多的孩子在进入幼儿园时做好更充分的准备。

sentences.en: So they are making some investments.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实进行了一些投资。

sentences.en: And when I did sort of back-of-the-envelope math, none of those things were like dramatically changing the picture of how much Mississippi was spending per student.
sentences.zh: 当我做了一个大致的估算时，发现这些并没有根本性地改变密西西比州生均支出的整体面貌。

sentences.en: But it was targeted and it allowed the State Department of Education to make specific investments versus allowing districts to spend it however they want.
sentences.zh: 但它是定向投入，这让州教育部能够进行具体的投资，而不是任由各学区随意花钱。

sentences.en: It does seem to show that it's possible to make meaningful improvements in education without spending vast amounts of money.
sentences.zh: 这似乎确实表明，在不花大钱的情况下，也有可能在教育方面取得有意义的改善。

sentences.en: We've been talking about fourth grade test scores, Sarah.
sentences.zh: 萨拉，我们一直在讨论四年级的测试成绩。

sentences.en: What are we seeing in the later years?
sentences.zh: 我们在高年级看到了什么情况？

sentences.en: Do these improvements last in Mississippi?
sentences.zh: 这些进步在密西西比州持久吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is one of the criticisms of what's happening in Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是对密西西比州现状的批评之一。

sentences.en: When you get to eighth grade, the results start to look a little bit less impressive.
sentences.zh: 当你到了八年级时，结果开始显得没有那么亮眼了。

sentences.en: They still do quite well adjusted for the poverty and the students that they serve, but kids in Massachusetts are still way outperforming eighth graders in Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 考虑到贫困率以及他们所服务的学生群体，他们的表现仍然相当不错，但马萨诸塞州的孩子们的表现依然远远超过密西西比州的八年级学生。

sentences.en: And so the state is actually trying to take some of the things that they're doing in the early years and trying to apply it to older kids.
sentences.zh: 因此，该州实际上正试图将他们在低年级采取的一些做法应用到年龄较大的孩子身上。

sentences.en: So they're trying to get more money for adolescent literacy coaches, like the same thing they do in the early grades.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正试图为青少年识字辅导员争取更多资金，就像他们在低年级做的那样。

sentences.en: They're trying to do that so that the bottom performing schools in late elementary school and middle school could also get literacy coaches, things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图这样做，以便小学高年级和初中里表现垫底的学校也能拥有识字辅导员，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So basically, part of it is Mississippi is not applying these interventions consistently every single year.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，部分原因在于密西西比州并没有在每一年都始终如一地应用这些干预措施。

sentences.en: This is an early education strategy that they're applying.
sentences.zh: 这是一项他们正在应用的早期教育策略。

sentences.en: And they're saying, we would need to do this on the long haul to actually see the results carry over.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们需要长期坚持这样做，才能真正看到成果得以延续。

sentences.en: Now, I should mention that just last year on the state tests for the first time outside of the pandemic, Mississippi started to see a little bit of a dip in its scores.
sentences.zh: 现在我必须提一下，就在去年，除疫情期间外，密西西比州在州级测试中首次开始看到成绩出现小幅下滑。

sentences.en: And so we don't know what that's going to look like on the national tests that allow you to compare across states.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道在那些可以进行跨州对比的全国性测试中，结果会是什么样子。

sentences.en: But it is a little bit of a something, a little inclination of is Mississippi starting to stagnate or is it just dealing with the same issues that everyone else is around the
sentences.zh: 但这确实有点迹象，让人不禁猜测密西西比州是开始停滞不前了，还是说它只是在应对全国各地其他地方都面临的相同问题

sentences.en: country when it comes to students missing school, post-pandemic, some of the things with technology and screens.
sentences.zh: 比如疫情后学生旷课的问题，以及科技产品和屏幕带来的一些影响。

sentences.en: And is that affecting students' learning?
sentences.zh: 这是否正在影响学生的学习？

sentences.en: So it's like, look at what it's taken so far.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比，看看目前为止付出了多少代价。

sentences.en: And also, can this be sustained when you look at the tides that are facing education nationally?
sentences.zh: 而且，面对全国教育界面临的大环境，这种做法能否持续下去？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So there are some caveats here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一些需要注意的地方。

sentences.en: This Mississippi miracle is not 100 percent durable.
sentences.zh: 这个“密西西比奇迹”并不是百分之百持久的。

sentences.en: It does seem, though, that Mississippi has figured something out that other states haven't about educating kids, about specifically educating poor kids in this case.
sentences.zh: 不过看起来，密西西比州确实摸索出了一套其他州尚未掌握的教育孩子的门道，特别是在这个案例中是如何教育贫困儿童的。

sentences.en: This is a deep red state following through on a goal that I think blue states would say they value a lot, being the best at lifting up the most disadvantaged children.
sentences.zh: 这是一个深红州，正在贯彻一个我认为蓝州也会声称非常重视的目标，那就是成为提升最多弱势儿童水平的佼佼者。

sentences.en: And so I wonder, are there other states that are looking at this and wondering if they should mimic it, if they should try this?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，是否有其他州正在关注这一点，并琢磨着是否应该效仿，是否应该尝试这种做法？

sentences.en: Well, there are some states that are showing some similar signs of progress, but there are generally a few handful of other red states in the South.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实有些州表现出了一些类似的进步迹象，但大体上是南部地区的少数几个红州。

sentences.en: So Louisiana and Alabama have also shown some promising signs over the last few years using some of the same strategies as Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 因此，路易斯安那州和阿拉巴马州在过去几年里也采用了一些与密西西比州相同的策略，并显示出了一些有希望的迹象。

sentences.en: Maryland is another state that comes to mind.
sentences.zh: 马里兰州是另一个让人想到的州。

sentences.en: They've actually hired Mississippi's former state superintendent who helped lead this turnaround.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至聘请了密西西比州前州教育总监，正是她协助引领了这次翻身仗。

sentences.en: So she's now in Maryland trying to help Maryland, which was once number two in the country for reading and fell way to the bottom, basically do Mississippi 2.0 up there.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在正在马里兰州努力帮助马里兰州——该州曾一度在全国阅读水平排名第二，后来却跌至垫底——基本上要在那里打造一个“密西西比2.0版”。

sentences.en: Help them pull a Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 帮他们搞一个密西西比式的逆袭。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: But by and large, blue states, I agree with you, should sort of be looking at, wow, what is
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，蓝州，我同意你的看法，应该好好看看，哇，密西西比州在做什么？

sentences.en: Mississippi doing?
sentences.zh: 密西西比州在做什么？

sentences.en: What is Louisiana and Alabama doing?
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州和阿拉巴马州在做什么？

sentences.en: What should we be doing?
sentences.zh: 我们应该做些什么？

sentences.en: And we haven't quite seen the same embrace of some of these policies.
sentences.zh: 而我们还没有看到他们对其中一些政策表现出同样的拥护。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Well, one reason is that lots of blue states are contending with powerful political forces like the teachers unions in states like, you know, California, New York, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，原因之一是许多蓝州正在与强大的政治力量进行较量，比如像加利福尼亚州、纽约州、马萨诸塞州等地的教师工会。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Teachers unions have historically opposed some of the strong test-based accountability measures like we see in Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 教师工会历来反对一些像我们在密西西比州看到的以测试为基础的强力问责措施。

sentences.en: And they have a lot of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 他们对此有很多理由。

sentences.en: But I think the reality is it's just harder to make sweeping top-down radical change when you're dealing with negotiations and political forces that it just makes things a lot more
sentences.zh: 但我认为现实情况是，当你需要应对各种谈判和政治力量时，想要进行全面、自上而下的激进变革就变得更加困难，这让事情复杂化了。

sentences.en: complicated.
sentences.zh: 事情复杂得多。

sentences.en: And then, you know, another reason is that blue states have gone in a different direction over the past few years.
sentences.zh: 然后呢，你知道，另一个原因是蓝州在过去几年里走向了不同的方向。

sentences.en: In some cases, between the pandemic and other things, they've lowered proficiency standards.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，在经历疫情和其他事情期间，他们降低了熟练度标准。

sentences.en: They've gotten rid of graduation requirements.
sentences.zh: 他们取消了毕业要求。

sentences.en: They've been much more focused on what a source of mind likes to call the inputs of education.
sentences.zh: 他们更加专注于我的一位思想来源喜欢称之为教育投入的东西。

sentences.en: Like, we're going to add counselors and social workers, and we're going to increase spending, and those are things that schools need and they want and kids need.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们要增加辅导员和社工，我们要增加开支，这些都是学校需要、想要而且孩子们需要的。

sentences.en: But it's more of a conversation about the inputs than the outputs, such as, you know, how are kids doing on the test?
sentences.zh: 但这更多的是关于投入的讨论，而不是产出的讨论，比如，你知道，孩子们在测试中表现如何？

sentences.en: Are they prepared?
sentences.zh: 他们准备好了吗？

sentences.en: And in Mississippi, I think there's much more agreement that academics is core, and that is what a school is for.
sentences.zh: 而在密西西比州，我认为大家更有共识，即学术是核心，这才是学校存在的目的。

sentences.en: You know, one of the ironies in all of this is this red state, Mississippi, is taking an
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里面最大的讽刺之一就是，这个红州密西西比州，采取了一种在很多方面看起来可以被认为是大政府式的策略。

sentences.en: approach that feels in many ways like it could be considered a big government type of strategy.
sentences.zh: 州政府某种程度上剥夺了学校的地方控制权，将自己的优先事项强加给独立教师和家庭，采取了强力干预的做法。

sentences.en: The state government kind of taking away local control from the schools and forcing its priorities on individual teachers and on families, like taking a heavy hand in things.
sentences.zh: 强力干预各种事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's sort of the opposite of what you would think.
sentences.zh: 是的，这和你的想法恰恰相反。

sentences.en: And then you have states like Oregon, who's, you know, deep blue state, a lot of liberal values, and it has taken the opposite approach in many ways.
sentences.zh: 然后你再看看像俄勒冈州这样的州，你知道，这是一个深蓝州，有着许多自由主义价值观，它在很多方面采取了截然相反的方法。

sentences.en: It is much more hands-off when it comes to their education department and telling districts what to do.
sentences.zh: 在教育部门以及对各学区指手画脚方面，它要放权得多。

sentences.en: It takes a much softer approach to accountability.
sentences.zh: 它对问责制采取了一种温和得多的方法。

sentences.en: There's a lot of distrust of testing in the state, of standardized testing.
sentences.zh: 该州对测试、对标准化测试存在着极大的不信任。

sentences.en: And at the same time, they're getting a much poorer return on investment on the money that they spend.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们在所花费的资金上得到的投资回报率却要低得多。

sentences.en: When you adjust for their demographics and who they serve, Oregon is at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 当你根据他们的人口统计数据和他们服务的对象进行调整时，俄勒冈州是垫底的。

sentences.en: And so it is a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: It's very much the inverse of what you would expect.
sentences.zh: 这完全是你所预料情况的对立面。

sentences.en: Just to step back here, Sarah, from all your reporting on Mississippi, on its success on these measures, what is the lesson of this little red state that could?
sentences.zh: 萨拉，抛开你对密西西比州及其在这些指标上取得成功的全部报道不谈，这个能干的小红州给我们带来了什么启示？

sentences.en: What should we take from this?
sentences.zh: 我们应该从中汲取什么经验？

sentences.en: Well, I think one of the clear lessons is that it is possible to make progress, and poverty cannot be an excuse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为清晰的教训之一就是，取得进步是完全可能的，贫困绝不能成为借口。

sentences.en: Like, number one, this is possible.
sentences.zh: 第一，这是做得到的。

sentences.en: So then the question is, how do you do it?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，你该怎么做？

sentences.en: You know, one of the things is just that there is no magic bullet and that you have to do this and this and this, and you have to keep after it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中一点就是世上没有灵丹妙药，你必须这样做、这样做、再这样做，而且必须坚持不懈地推进。

sentences.en: Like, it's not something where you can just pick the easiest thing that's most politically palatable.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是那种你可以只挑选最简单、最符合政治利益的事情去做的领域。

sentences.en: And when I look around the country and I look at discussions about education, it strikes me
sentences.zh: 当我环顾全国并观察关于教育的讨论时，我深有感触

sentences.en: that it's not going to be politically popular to promise results and change in education because
sentences.zh: 在教育领域承诺带来成果和变革在政治上是吃力不讨好的，因为

sentences.en: it just takes a really long time to see real progress, even when you are doing everything that you can and all of the strategies.
sentences.zh: 即使你已经竭尽全力、用尽了所有的策略，要看到真正的进步也需要非常长的时间。

sentences.en: Think about it.
sentences.zh: 想想看。

sentences.en: You've got a two-term governor that's eight years.
sentences.zh: 你有一位两届任期的州长，也就是八年。

sentences.en: I mean, you might start to see some progress in that time, but maybe not.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在那期间你可能开始看到一些进展，但也可能没有。

sentences.en: And so what you really have to have is the political will and the will across business and
sentences.zh: 所以你真正需要拥有的是政治意愿，以及整个商业界和

sentences.en: across the culture of a place to say, like, this is something that we as a state are going to commit to.
sentences.zh: 地方文化中上下同欲的决心，去宣告：这就是我们作为一个州将要全力以赴的事情。

sentences.en: We're going to be pretty aggressive.
sentences.zh: 我们要采取相当激进的行动。

sentences.en: We're going to be a little bossy in telling you what to do.
sentences.zh: 我们在对你们发号施令时可能会显得有点专断。

sentences.en: But then we're also going to flood you with support and we're going to see it through to the end.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我们也会向你们倾注海量的支持，并且我们会把这件事彻底贯彻到底。

sentences.en: Well, Sarah, thanks so much for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 好的，萨拉，非常感谢你做客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 我是韦娜·刘。

sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色听症的现象。

sentences.en: and Iran.
sentences.zh: 以及伊朗。

sentences.zh: 该声明是在内塔尼亚胡表示已下令以色列政府就解除真主党武装人员武装与黎巴嫩展开外交会谈数小时后发出的。

sentences.en: President Trump told NBC News that after he called Netanyahu, the Israeli leader had agreed to scale back his strikes on Lebanon.

sentences.zh: 还有，下午好。

sentences.zh: 将我与声名狼藉的杰弗里·爱泼斯坦联系在一起的谎言今天必须停止。

sentences.en: Melania Trump delivered a rare public address from the White House, criticizing what she called false claims about her relationship to Jeffrey Epstein.
sentences.zh: 梅拉尼娅·特朗普在白宫发表了一场罕见的公开演讲，批评她所谓的关于她与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦关系的虚假指控。

sentences.en: I am not Epstein's victim.
sentences.zh: 我不是爱泼斯坦的受害者。

sentences.en: Epstein did not introduce me to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 爱泼斯坦没有把我介绍给唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: It was unclear why the First Lady decided to speak out at this particular moment, or what reports she was specifically referring to.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚第一夫人为何决定在这个特定时刻发声，或者她具体指的是哪些报道。

sentences.en: She addressed a cordial email that she'd sent to Ghislaine Maxwell and run-ins that she'd
sentences.zh: 她谈到了她曾发给吉斯莱恩·麦克斯韦的一封亲切邮件以及她与爱泼斯坦的偶遇

sentences.en: had with Epstein, but hit back hard at any insinuation that she was connected to Epstein or
sentences.zh: 有过接触，但她强烈反击了任何暗示她与爱泼斯坦或

sentences.en: Maxwell's crimes.
sentences.zh: 麦克斯韦的罪行有关的影射。

sentences.en: I was not a participant, was never on Epstein's plane, and never visited his private island.
sentences.zh: 我不是参与者，从未登上过爱泼斯坦的飞机，也从未去过他的私人岛屿。

sentences.en: The First Lady called on Congress to keep investigating Epstein.
sentences.zh: 第一夫人呼吁国会继续调查爱泼斯坦。
